etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English, from Late Latin corōllārium (“money paid for a garland; gift, gratuity, corollary; consequence, deduction”), from corōlla (“small garland”), diminutive of corōna (“crown”).
senses: A gift beyond what is actually due; an addition or superfluity.
An a fortiori occurrence, as a result of another effort without significant additional effort.
Occurring as a natural consequence or result; attendant; consequential.
(rare) Forming a proposition that follows from one already proved.
